text: The GOAT debates involving different eras are stupid because they ignore the evolution of greatness One aspect of the GOAT debates when comparing different eras is how conveniently the entire process of evolution is consciously or subconsciously ignored. You don’t get all of the features of the new Corvette immediately. It is a process of evolution and improvement. It takes multiple greats that were great and revolutionary in their own eras first along the way. Just as vehicular technology improves so too does sports science, nutrition, video technology, analytics, and basketball training technology. The access to these improvements also reaches people younger than it used to at lower price points. What used to be only available once you made it to the NCAA or NBA in previous eras is being experienced by more sooner. Expectations change. Star players from the 1980s didn’t shoot threes at the rate Steph Curry did because nobody thought that was smart back then. It doesn’t mean those greats couldn’t have learned to shoot more 3s if they’d been raised in the current era after. Expectations evolve and now the 3PAs Steph took earlier in his career look far less extreme than they once did. In the future there will be a new shooter who takes and probably makes even more. When new coaches and GMs see what is possible in systems featuring previous generational stars who broke the mold they seek out young talents who remind them of those previous greats and mold them. They seek to emulate what worked before. They encourage similar play. They teach it. They show video. This all happens at a younger age than what came before and so the next greats benefit from all of the success previous greats highlighted as effective. They’re invested in and developed because of the success seen previously of the era’s most unstoppable talents. We see this in copy cat phases. Centers who can score down low are all the rage. Then scoring wings. Then PGs who shoot 3s at elite rates while creating for everyone else. The future greats are all molded, shaped, invested in, sought after, and built around because of the players who reminded of them before that were dominant.
